place.source_title: Harbour Town Store (storefront with a false front)

brief: A narrow two-storey clapboard store with a tall false front, a big display window with bunting and a striped awning, a hanging sign and flower baskets. One photo. Older than 1970: Lake Erie island and harbour-town main streets (the Put-in-Bay model) are 19th-century commercial blocks; no newer example of this main-street type exists. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: a false-front frame store (Vermilion OH, 1880s), now an eatery: a square clapboard false front with a plain cornice, a yellow awning, two big windows with lettering either side of a centre door, flag bunting, window boxes, corn stalks for autumn
